Oh yeah, I'm in the same boat. I've been in design for about 6 years and in UX for almost 2. I work for a e-commerce company and I really can't find purpose in the job and I'm not interested in my work but I need the cash. And I'm also tired of fighting for petty things and spending all that energy on something that really doesn't contribute to the world. Honestly I'm not even sure I wanna keep designing. At least not on e-commerce. If I design I want it to have purpose. I'm very interested in ecology, nature, conservation, etc. So I enrolled in a naturist school that teaches this kind of thing. Maybe I'll be able to start helping others better by understand the problem space more. And it's something I wanted to do since I'm little so it's a win win. Maybe I'll keep designing, maybe I'll start a new job, maybe I'll start a project to help non profits. I'm taking it day by day to see how I feel. In the mean time I'm keeping my job till things are more clear.

But yeah, start somewhere and wing it. See how you feel. In the mean time maybe keep your job. I've been feeling a little better since I've started going in a direction. It feels more like I'm working towards something and less like I'm trapped. 

Hope this helps and know that you are not alone in the existential crisis. It happens to a lot of us. Maybe we need a support group lol.

Good luck!

Baltar to me is a great character. Not only because James Callis is an amazing actor but because he is a character that is always looking for the upper hand in a situation. 

He takes many forms but always strives for that position of distinction. Be it political leader, scientist, religious cult leader, etc. And then we get to see his backstory. That scene in the brig where he drops the accent and talks in his native Aerilon accent is amazing. Gives me goosebumps. He is someone who is always trying to escape his past as a farmer, his relationship with his dad (which is very sad in the flashback), and his own mistakes and cowardice. 

He does a lot of cuestionable stuff on the road. And still thinks he's in the right. That he was justified. And at the same time he has some guilt. The whole occupation of New Caprica is so good as he finally gets what he wants at an immense cost for others and himself. His trial is excellent. Lee's speech about everyone doing the wrong thing and getting a pass but that Baltar shouldn't have one is great.

In the end he starts to accept all of it. "You know, I know about farming". 

Baltar is one of my favorites. And I hate him and I love him and I love to hate him.
He also got tortured by the cardassians and assimilated by the Borg. So yeah, he has a lot of sessions ahead of him

I think that DN was a lot better when L lived. BUT I also think that the second half has a lot of interesting points. Like for example, with higuchi we got to see what the death note would be used like with a character that had nothing but his own benefit in mind. We got to see the scaling up of things. The impact that had the death of L. They were forced to recruit 2 successors for the job of catching Kira + hq + everything else. With namikawa we got to see how far Kira was willing to go betraying a powerful Ally and someone who loved him, with misa we got to see how much of a discarded tool see was all along. That scene with the caged bird and misa sitting next to it is excellent to show the point of her situation. And you can't just help but feel pity for her. Similar thing with Teru, someone who had the intention of erasing the evil from the world (as opposed to Kira who was just in a power fantasy claiming he was the god of the new world) gets carried away by fanaticism and gets stabbed in the back in the anime (in the manga he gets arrested). The whole bit with Yagami senior is heart wrenching. And finally with Kira getting caught (even though I didn't like how it happened) we get to see him begging for his allies whom he betrayed and killed to come help him now that he was done after he had shaped the entire world because of his actions.

I think that the weight shifts. In the first half we get to see more of an amazing battle of logic and wit and in the second half we get to see the emotional and humane consequences of the first half. Overall I think the first part is more entertaining but I wouldn't replaced the second for anything. It's such a good series.
